p: they should not become impure from their outer
earthenware vessels and vessels made from natron … neter … their impurity are equal … they become impure
earthenware vessels and vessels made from natron [neter], the halakhot of their impurity are equal in that they become impure
and, … they render … impure from their air … And they become impure from behind, … do not become impure from their outer … And the breaking … renders them pure.

and, once impure, they render food that enters their airspace impure from their air space. And they become impure from behind, i.e., if a primary source of impurity enters into the bottom of the vessel, where there is an empty space and a receptacle, the vessel becomes impure. However, earthenware vessels do not become impure from their outer side, i.e., if a primary source of impurity came into contact with the outer side of the vessel, the inside of the vessel does not become impure. And the breaking of earthenware vessels renders them pure.
natron vessels and earthenware vessels are those whose … impurity are equal,
natron vessels and earthenware vessels are those whose halakhot of impurity are equal,
